title: Choose the portfolio's visual world
question: I can build this as a project-select world or take one of these alternate directions. Pick the one that feels most like your work.

options.label: World Select
options.lineage: RPG world maps and level-select screens
options.thesis: The portfolio opens like choosing what to explore next.
options.viewport: A large game preview fills the stage; a connected project route and short personal introduction frame it.
options.risk: A literal game menu could turn the projects into a gimmick if the work stops leading.

raised.raise: A limited, committed palette carries whole regions instead of scattering accents.
The selected project has an unmistakable, keyboard-accessible state.
The path through projects has a deliberate focal point and clear next stop.
One project owns the opening viewport with real impact.
Small drawn marks can reflect the creator without becoming a mascot theme.

options.label: Indie Game Library
options.lineage: personal game shelves and launcher libraries
options.thesis: A small, honest library of things made and things still being tried.
options.viewport: One featured game sits beside a tighter shelf of experiments, with its playable link immediately visible.
options.risk: This is familiar portfolio territory and needs strong project imagery to feel personal.

options.label: Project Sleeves
options.lineage: Blue Note session sleeves translated to game and art covers
options.thesis: Each project arrives as a bold cover made from its own imagery.
options.viewport: A sharply cropped game frame cuts into a full-width color field; project titles become the navigation.
options.case: Creative work reads strongly as a collection of authored covers, though the jazz reference is farther from game making.
options.risk: The cover grammar must stay flexible across games, software screenshots, mods, and art.

options.label: Riso Studio
options.thesis: The site feels like a personal stack of printed work in progress.
options.viewport: Game frames interrupt large printed color shapes, with the active project pulled to the front.
options.case: The personal, experimental tone fits; paper and text could pull the result back toward the article feel you dislike.
options.risk: It needs restrained copy and strong project imagery to remain a portfolio.

options.label: Step Sequencer
options.thesis: Projects become steps in a loop.
options.viewport: A row of selectable project steps below a game preview.
options.case: Its control grammar is precise, but a music instrument does not explain this collection of work.
options.risk: The portfolio could look like an unrelated tool.
options.kept: A clear selected state and keyboard interaction.

options.label: Garden Vistas
options.thesis: Projects unfold as a series of vistas.
options.viewport: A central path leads from one project view to another.
options.case: The visual reference is too remote from the work to identify the creator quickly.
options.risk: Visitors may have to learn the metaphor before finding projects.
options.kept: A deliberate focal point and next stop.

options.label: Forged Metal
options.thesis: Each project lands like one strike.
options.viewport: A full-width project reveal occupies the screen.
options.case: Its force is useful, but the industrial world obscures this maker's range.
options.risk: The form would overpower the projects.
options.kept: Let one real project own the opening viewport.

options.label: Character Sheet
options.thesis: A drawn character introduces each kind of work.
options.viewport: A central illustrated mascot sits above project variants.
options.case: The creator's actual projects deserve the central position more than a new character.
options.risk: It could imply a mascot identity that is not established.
options.kept: Allow small personal marks without hiding the work.

canonCard.label: Classic Portfolio
canonCard.thesis: A polished grid of projects with simple section navigation.
canonCard.viewport: A brief introduction above a featured project and regular gallery.
canonCard.risk: It is easy to understand but less individual.
